creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing

Short-Time Fourier Transform
Spectrogram
Window Functions
description: The short-time Fourier transform of a chirp, a frequency-shift-keyed signal or a note sequence is computed with a radix-2 FFT and drawn as a spectrogram, with a waveform, a time cursor and the spectrum of the frame at the cursor. Sliders for window length and overlap show the trade-off between time resolution and frequency resolution.

educational.topic: Spectrograms and the time-frequency resolution trade-off of the STFT
learningObjectives: Explain why a spectrogram is needed for a signal whose frequency content changes with time
Compute the time span, bin spacing and hop size of an STFT from the window length, sampling rate and overlap
Analyze how the window length trades time resolution against frequency resolution
Choose STFT settings that suit a given signal
prerequisites: The DFT, bin spacing and window functions

controls.label: Signal
options: Note sequence (C5 E5 G5 C6 G5)

controls.label: Click or drag in the waveform or spectrogram to move the time cursor; point at the spectrogram for a time, frequency and level readout

equations: X[m, k] = sum over n of x[n + m H] w[n] e^(-j 2 pi k n / N)
time span of the window = N / fs, bin spacing = fs / N, product = 1
hop H = N (1 - overlap), frames = floor((Ns - N) / H) + 1
assumptions: fs = 8000 Hz and the signal is 8000 samples (1 s) long
The FFT length equals the window length (no zero-padding), so each bin is drawn as one cell
Each frame is plotted at the centre of its N samples; times where no complete window fits are left blank
Levels are scaled so that a steady bin-centred sinusoid of amplitude 1 reads 0 dB; the dB scale spans 80 dB
All three signals are synthesized; no recorded speech or music is used

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Change one STFT parameter at a time and relate the shape of the time-frequency cells to the computed resolutions
keyQuestions: Why can the window not be both short in time and narrow in frequency?
Does more overlap improve the resolution of a spectrogram?
Why is the longest window not the best one for a chirp?
commonMisconceptions: A longer window always gives a better spectrogram
Increasing the overlap improves time resolution
The spectrogram shows the exact frequency of a signal at each instant
assessmentOpportunities: Compute the time span and bin spacing for each window length and verify their product
Choose and justify a window length for reading FSK bits and another for separating musical notes
